notes: Built from sc-t633-electrode-cleaning-01, sc-no-nitric-acid-01 (turn 1) and sc-hcl-soak-01 (turn 2). Turn 2 - 'How long can it sit in that before we are doing more harm than good, and then what?' - has no standalone subject: both 'it' and 'that' are bare back-references to the probe and the acid named only in turn 1, so the turn is dead on its own. Shape is procedure-then-its-limit. expected_to_favor is 'rag': the vendor datasheet is inside the slice and says only that hard coatings should be removed chemically using the manufacturer's own cleaner (SLICE-EXCLUSION line 38), so a slice-bound arm will produce a fluent, useless answer and will not have the strength, the excluded reagents, the soak ceiling or the rinse. That partial-but-wrong failure is what this fixture is meant to expose. Turn 1 is written to assume the vendor answer has already run out, so the fixture cannot be satisfied from the slice.

turns.content: Our salt sensor has been reading low and a soft brush around the electrodes didn't bring it back. The vendor sheet just says to clean it chemically without saying what with. What do the field manuals put you in?

must_contain: says to start with a detergent solution and only escalate to acid if that fails
names dilute hydrochloric acid, at about 5 percent, as the acid to escalate to
says to check the instrument manufacturer's own guidance before putting any acid on the probe
warns that nitric acid, aqua regia and anything else that etches platinum or gold must not be used, because they will attack platinum and platinum-iridium electrodes
must_not: recommends an acid or concentration the sources do not give
recommends abrasive mechanical cleaning of the electrode surfaces
answers only with the vendor's proprietary probe cleaner and stops there

turns.content: How long can it sit in that before we're doing more harm than good, and then what?

must_contain: gives 2 hours as the maximum soak
states that the probe is rinsed thoroughly with deionized water afterwards
repeats or upholds that the manufacturer's recommendations govern, so a shorter limit from the instrument maker wins
must_not: invents a soak time longer than the source gives
says an overnight or open-ended soak is acceptable
omits the deionized-water rinse after the soak
answers about calibration-standard soak or storage instead of the acid clean
gives the ORP probe datasheet's few-minute hydrochloric acid soak as the conductivity probe's soak limit
